title: Proactive sampled eval fabric for catalog and tenant pin events
creator: Marco Li
description: Background: When catalog or customer-pinned model versions change we must detect quality regressions quickly without excessive cost. Existing flows trigger full-fidelity eval runs or ad-hoc smoke tests which are either slow or expensive. Goal: implement a lightweight, tenant-aware sampled eval fabric that automatically activates on pin/upgrade events and provides a prioritized, cost-bound set of checks (synthetic smoke -> sampled fidelity probes -> targeted differential tests). Scope: event listener for catalog + tenant pin events, sampling policy engine, fanout to synthetic runners, result aggregation and impact scoring, dashboard + alerting. Out of scope: full-scale nightly evaluation pipelines and human-driven manual evals.
acceptance_criteria: Pin/upgrade events in catalog and tenant model locks produce a sampled eval job within 2 minutes
Sampling policy applies tenant priority and recent-traffic heuristics (can be configured per-tenant)
Aggregated impact score (0-100) computed and stored with links to the failing prompt samples
Critical regressions (impact >= 70 by default) open an incident-like alert and create a remediation task
End-to-end cost of sampled evals remains within configured budget cap per event (default $50/event)
Results surfaced in Console under 'Pin Eval Results' with per-tenant filtering and raw artifacts download
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal catalog-only rollout (canary 5 models) + synthetic-only probes
Phase 2: tenant-aware sampling enabled for 10 pilot customers (opt-in flag)
Phase 3: GA enablement with adjustable per-tenant budget and SLA buckets
Fallback: if runner capacity unavailable, automatically fallback to minimal smoke checks and notify owners
monitoring: Dashboard: Pin Eval Results (filters: tenant, catalog, model-version, impact-score)
Alert: Pin-eval-critical when impact_score >= 70 and failing_count >= 5 in 15m
Log: archived raw responses for 30 days for audits
cost_guard: Budget cap per event default $50 (configurable). CI will reject enabling full-fidelity probes if projected cost > 5x default without explicit approval.
